P1.evidence: The rep's standard open: 'I've seen your application. It's very interesting. However, I'm kind of an old school guy. So walk me through what's been going on. What have you tried before? And like, what's the main thing that you're looking to fix right now?' The open question is strong and does double duty into P4, but the application is again named rather than read back, and no frame or frame agreement was set — which cost him at the end, when the prospect controlled the close by announcing his own timeline.

P2.evidence: Age was actually asked here — 'And how old are you right now?' — which is the only time in this batch, though height and weight still arrived unprompted. Work was worked properly, from 'Is that the seven years that you've been building your companies?' through to establishing he had stood up twice all day. Current training was asked directly ('So are you currently right now going to the gym or doing anything?') and diet was opened cleanly. The injury questioning is the weak point and it is the most consequential: the prospect volunteered two bulging discs, two stretched knee ligaments and shoulder impingement, and the rep's only contribution was an assertion — 'I'm gonna mind-read you right now, and I can assume that lower back, hips, traps, all of that is stiff.' He never asked how long, never asked what a clinician has said, never asked what movements are contraindicated. Health conditions, sleep and energy were not raised at all.

P3.evidence: The headline goal was asked cleanly — 'for you, what would be the biggest needle mover? What's the biggest goal?' — and produced 'pain-free' rather than a weight number, which is the right answer to have surfaced. The can't-do-it question was pushed properly: 'Picking up, that's one thing, but... one year from now' drew out 'I got to run after a kid'. The drive to family landed hard and in the prospect's own words: 'before it was just on me, but now there's a kid on the way, it's more than just me.' The reflect-back also landed — 'you're here and I think you understand that you cannot go longer like this' met with 'Oh, yeah, for sure. The self-awareness is there. I just got to put it into action.' Marked down because the deeper bridge was delivered as an assertion ('when your focus is so spread out... there is no gas in the tank for yourself') rather than asked, and the moving-better consequence was never raised.

P4.evidence: The best root-cause work in the batch and the only phase in these twelve files that is properly complete. What he tried came out in full (75 Hard, sporadic gym returns, gym-bro splits, dumbbells only). What happened was traced through the whole arc — 284 to 223 to 260. Why it did not stick was asked directly: 'you mentioned that consistency was, like, an issue in the past. Why is that? Because of the amount of work that you had, or what?' Then the gap question — 'So what was the biggest missing piece, like the accountability from someone?' — and crucially the rep let the prospect correct him rather than accepting his own suggested answer: 'No, so again, the first and biggest is the consistency due to either A, the lifestyle just became not realistic to maintain, and B, the injuries.' Only P4f is short: the information-isn't-the-problem framing was never put explicitly.

P5.evidence: A future-projection question was attempted but aimed at aspiration rather than consequence, and it came out garbled: 'Picking up, that's one thing, but, I don't know, 10 years from now, want to, like, 10 years, like, one year from now.' Nothing else ran — no what-does-life-look-like-in-two-years, no willingness to settle, no why not, no line in the sand. This is the phase that decided the call. When price hesitation arrived, the script says return to Phase 5, and there was no Phase 5 to return to; the rep had a 34-year-old carrying 65 lb above his athletic weight with two bulging discs and a baby arriving in weeks, and never once asked him to picture two more years of the same.

P6.evidence: Correct sequencing for once — the commitment ask came at 00:15:35, before any of the pillars were presented: 'first of all, I would need commitment from you, that you will show up and do the work... Are you willing to show up?' The prospect gave a real answer ('I have to at this point... there's a kid on the way, it's more than just me') and the rep sharpened it well with 'You don't have to do anything, man.' But this only tested willingness to work, not belief that the programme can deliver — the P6a belief question was never asked, which is exactly the gap that reappeared as 'I don't know if I'm getting that same one-on-one'. And when hesitation surfaced later the rep did not return to Phase 5 as the check requires.

P11.evidence: No close was reached. The prospect deferred to Friday and the call ended with a phone number exchange. Nothing to collect, schedule, sign or send.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:31:35 — 'Give me until tomorrow and I'll give you a response if I want to move forward or not.' Two scripted moves ran, and ran well: 'What's coming up that you don't want to go forward right now?' surfaced the real objection, and 'what's going to be the main factor that's going to pull the scale to one or to the other' surfaced that he plans to re-approach his old trainers first. Everything after that was skipped — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to pain-free', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now'. The prospect set the deadline, the rep accepted it, and the call ended.

A value-at-equal-price objection with no scripted play: remote coaching at $6,000 against in-person one-to-one functional training at about $1,500 a month that he has used before and rated highly. The rep improvised three reasonable counters — kettlebell expertise is scarce, in-person costs him time he does not have, and the equipment requirement is one bell — but missed the decisive one, which the prospect had already supplied. $1,500 a month across the same six months is $9,000, so the programme is a third cheaper than the alternative he is comparing it to, and the 'plus or minus that same amount of money' premise is simply wrong. Nobody did that arithmetic out loud. This is the same script gap logged against the Badrane Hriouch call, but inverted: the substitute here is more expensive, not cheaper, and the script still has nothing for it.

A provider-trust objection with no scripted play. The prospect explained his construction retainage habit — 'I keep 10% hanging... if I pay them in full, it's going to take them three business days to respond to my phone call' — as a reason not to pay in full. The rep answered it in one move by conceding a 50/50 split with interest waived, before any financial-picture questions and before testing whether trust or value was the real blocker. It resolved the stated concern, but it resolved it by giving away terms rather than by building confidence in delivery, and it created a pricing deviation in the process.

notes: Best root-cause work in the batch, and it went nowhere because the consequence frame that converts it into urgency was skipped again. The prospect handed over everything needed — an 80 lb gain, a failed 65 lb loss, chronic pain at 34, a first child due in weeks — and none of it was ever turned back on him as a cost of standing still. Two specific fixes: run the arithmetic on a competitor anchor before conceding the comparison, and stop offering interest-free splits, which is now twice in two days and directly contradicts what the manager said in the 1-1 the day before.
